title: THE D.B. COOPER MYSTERY | Part 2: The Jump
description:
Seattle, 1971. The money is on board, the passengers are free, and the hijacker gives his strangest orders yet. At 8:13 p.m., somewhere over the forests of Washington, he vanished into a storm.

Part 2 of an animated true-crime series about the D.B. Cooper case.

#dbcooper #truecrime #unsolvedmystery #animation #mystery

series.name: The D.B. Cooper Mystery
series.previously: A quiet man calling himself Dan Cooper hijacked Flight three-oh-five with a bomb in his briefcase. He demanded two hundred thousand dollars and four parachutes. And in Seattle, he asked about the rear stairs.

shots.say: In Seattle, the trade began. A canvas bag of cash and four parachutes came on board. In return, all thirty-six passengers walked off the plane.
A flight attendant carried the bag up the stairs. Ten thousand twenty-dollar bills. About twenty-one pounds of money.
He kept the two pilots, the flight engineer, and one flight attendant on board. Then he gave his new orders.
Fly toward Mexico City. Stay below ten thousand feet. Keep the landing gear down. Fly as slowly as possible. And leave the cabin unpressurized.
To an expert, those orders only made sense for one reason. Low, slow, and unpressurized, is exactly how you would fly if someone planned to jump.
The jet would need fuel, so they agreed on a stop in Reno, Nevada. At seven forty p.m., Flight three-oh-five took off again, into the night.
He sent the last flight attendant to the cockpit and told her to stay there. As she left, she saw him tying something around his waist.
She was the last person to ever see him.
shots.caption: THE LAST TIME.

shots.say: Outside, it was dark, raining, and below freezing. Beneath them, nothing but mountains and endless forest.

shots.caption: 8:00 PM
shots.say: Around eight p.m., a warning light flashed in the cockpit. The rear stairs had been opened.
The crew called back over the intercom and asked if he needed help. The answer was one word. No.
shots.caption: "NO."
8:13 PM
shots.say: At eight thirteen p.m., the crew felt a sudden bump in the tail of the plane.
Investigators believe that was the moment Dan Cooper jumped. Into a storm. At night. Wearing a business suit and loafers.
Somewhere below was southwest Washington. Thick forest. Freezing rain. And a wind that could carry a parachute for miles.
At ten fifteen p.m., the jet landed in Reno. Police and FBI agents surrounded it.
They searched the cabin. He was gone. So was the money. Left behind were two of the parachutes, a black clip-on tie, and a few cigarette butts.
A man had jumped out of an airliner, at night, with two hundred thousand dollars. And disappeared.
shots.caption: GONE.

shots.say: But one question has haunted investigators ever since. Did Dan Cooper survive that jump?
shots.caption: DID HE SURVIVE?
